name: GTx-027

lead: GTx-027 is an experimental SARM of the arylpropionamide class, investigated for breast cancer and stress urinary incontinence.
It is described as discontinued or preclinical, and no human trial on muscle or appearance has been published.

paras: SARMs are designed to activate androgen receptors selectively. Mouse research on SARMs reported increased pelvic floor muscle mass.
No human safety data are available in the sources reviewed. The SARM class is unapproved, banned by WADA, and linked in case reports to liver injury with recreational use.

Poster 390: Systematic Review of SARMs Abuse in Athletes

lead: GTx-027 is an investigational non-steroidal selective androgen receptor modulator (SARM) of the arylpropionamide class, associated with GTx, Inc. and investigated for breast cancer and stress urinary incontinence [1]. Wikipedia lists its status as Phase I, discontinued, or preclinical [1].

Published research on the compound is limited. A 2017 mouse study examined whether tissue-selective SARMs increase pelvic floor muscle mass in ovariectomized mice, motivated by the lack of oral treatments for stress urinary incontinence [2]. No appearance or physique trials exist.

paras: The pelvic floor is rich in androgen receptors, and researchers proposed SARMs as possible oral therapy for stress urinary incontinence; a 2017 study in ovariectomized mice reported that tissue-selective SARMs increased pelvic floor muscle mass [2]. The related SARM enobosarm did not meet its endpoint in a Phase II trial for stress urinary incontinence and was abandoned [1].

SARMs are not FDA approved but are sold online, and athletes' use has led to positive tests across several sports bodies, according to a 2023 systematic review poster [3]. WADA has banned the class since 2008 [1]. GTx-027 itself is not described as a common gray-market product in the sources reviewed.
No studies found. The available research on GTx-027's therapeutic area is preclinical, such as the mouse pelvic-floor study above [2].
